We review user access rights quarterly through a formal access recertification process, supported by an Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) platform that automates recertification workflows. Access changes require documented business justification and manager approval, under approval workflows defined in our Access Control Policy. Privileged access is further restricted through Privileged Access Management (PAM) tooling with session recording. When an employee is terminated, we deactivate all logical access within 4 hours of the termination event and revoke physical access on the same business day, following a documented offboarding checklist. Offboarding records are sampled during quarterly access reviews and annual audits.

We manage security patches on a defined cycle: critical patches are deployed within 24–72 hours of release, high-severity patches within 7 days, and routine patches within 30 days. Automated deployment is used for endpoints and servers where possible. Exceptions are tracked and risk-accepted by the CISO, and patch compliance is reviewed weekly, with non-compliant assets escalated through the vulnerability management workflow. Vulnerabilities are identified through continuous automated scanning, external penetration testing, threat intelligence feeds and vendor advisories, and are risk-rated using CVSS scoring. Findings are tracked in a centralized vulnerability management platform with remediation SLAs of 24 hours (Critical), 7 days (High) and 30 days (Medium). Mean time to remediate is reported monthly to senior leadership.

We integrate security into our CI/CD pipelines in several ways. Mandatory SAST and DAST scans run in CI/CD pipelines, and software composition analysis covers open-source dependencies. Pipelines, build servers and developer tooling are subject to the same security standards as production, including access controls, vulnerability scanning and secrets management. Secrets are held in a dedicated vault with dynamic secret generation where supported, and hardcoded credentials are detected through pre-commit hooks and pipeline scanning. Build modification rights are limited to authorized CI/CD service accounts, build artifacts are signed with code signing certificates traceable to an internal certificate authority, and artifact integrity is verified at each deployment stage. Pipeline configuration changes require security team review, and infrastructure drift from approved baselines triggers automated alerts.

We integrate software composition analysis (SCA) tooling into our CI/CD pipelines to identify known vulnerabilities in open-source and third-party libraries before deployment. We generate a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for all production applications and maintain it in our software asset inventory. Our build pipeline is hardened with access controls limiting modification rights to authorized CI/CD service accounts, and all build artifacts are signed using code signing certificates traceable to an internal certificate authority. We verify artifact integrity at each deployment stage, and pipeline configuration changes require security team review. Third-party build tool dependencies are managed through a curated internal package mirror subject to vulnerability scanning. When assessing vendor software, we review the vendor's SDLC security practices and SBOM availability.
